title: Maine, withroom to stay.
summary: A workable kitchen, swim things ready, and somewhere for the day to land.
search: The journalWells, MaineFamily field noteFrom our Wells getaway · a beach photograph, not a resort or pool photograph.Misty Harbor, Wells · Family field noteMaine, withroom to stay.A workable kitchen, swim things ready, and somewhere for the day to land.Come alongMake the poolthe main event.Misty Harbor was our base for a Wells getaway. Time in the water, food we could make ourselves, and a room to come back to gave the weekend its shape.Looking for practical details? From our family notebook · a Maine overnightA room that helps.There is a particular kind of relief in opening the door to a hotel room and realizing the room itself is going to help. Not merely look nice in photographs. Help. At Misty Harbor, the useful things were the lovely things: enough space to spread out without living out of a heap of bags, a kitchen that meant dinner did not have to become another outing, and the indoor pool waiting downstairs like a perfectly reasonable answer to the question, “What should we do now?”We have become suspicious of weekends that arrive with too many verbs. Visit. Shop. Tour. Reserve. Hurry. This one worked better because the list was short. We brought in the bags, made the suite feel familiar, found the chargers, put the swim things where we could actually find them again, and went to the water. That was the event. No one needed to earn it by sightseeing first.The original family story is retained from the earlier notebook; the decorative artwork is an interpretation.Put the swim things where you can find them.More from our weekend notebook +Wells is good for this kind of trip because Maine is outside the window even when you are not doing Maine particularly hard. The coast is close. There are places to get something easy to eat. You can take a drive, see the water, come back, and still feel as though you went somewhere. A swim can become the center of the afternoon instead of the leftover activity squeezed between adult plans.It is the kind of place we would choose again not because it asks to be remembered, but because it leaves room for the family to make the memory. That distinction matters to us more every year. Give us a clean landing place, a pool, a workable kitchen and the freedom to change the plan, and we can supply the rest. Dinner does not have to become another outing.What stayed with usSomewhere for the day to land.What we remember is not a checklist of attractions. It is the feeling of everybody having a little room around them. Wet swimsuits could dry. One person could be awake while another was finished with the day. We could make food without negotiating a restaurant. We could go back to the pool because, wonderfully, there was no rule saying the second swim did not count as an itinerary.We have learned not to confuse a full itinerary with a full weekend.That is increasingly our definition of a good family hotel: it gives the day somewhere to land. Misty Harbor did. The weekend felt simple, coastal, comfortable and ours—which, for us, is considerably better than impressive.This is our earlier family story. summary: The lighthouse gives the day its setting. The funny details make it ours.

The Nubble can be the destination without becoming a list of things to finish.Looking for practical details? From our family notebook · York, MaineThe view arrives first.York is very good at reminding us that an outing does not need a narrative arc. Sometimes the entire story is: we drove to the coast, we saw the ocean, somebody got an absurd Maine-shaped sweet, we looked at a lighthouse, and everyone went home with salt in their hair and the agreeable tiredness that comes from having actually been somewhere.The Nubble works especially well because so much of the pleasure arrives immediately. You do not have to hike for an hour before you earn the view. There it is: rock, water, white lighthouse, red roof, gulls doing what gulls do, and the ocean making everything else seem temporarily less important. You can stay a long time or a short time and the basic experience is still intact.The original family story is retained from the earlier notebook; the decorative artwork is an interpretation.Check the weather, the facilities and the way back.More from our York notebook +We like places where the person who wants to look can look, the person who wants to move can move, and the person who is ready to get back in the car has not ruined a carefully choreographed plan. York has enough around it to build a whole day, but it does not require one. That distinction has saved many family outings.The photograph we kept from York is not a formal lighthouse portrait. It is a small, funny family moment with a lobster-shaped sweet, which feels exactly right. The landmark gives the day its setting; the odd little details make it ours. That is what we are trying to preserve in these Favorite Places—not just where to go, but why the place stayed with us. Sometimes the souvenir is the absurd sweet.The details that stayedWhat the camera roll remembers.There are also small pleasures that become disproportionately memorable. A silly candy. Something cold to drink. A photograph taken at exactly the right moment. Standing by the rail and watching the water for another minute because nobody is rushing to the next reservation. Those details are the ones our camera roll remembers better than the itinerary ever does.We leave some Maine unvisited. It will be there next time.So our favorite York plan is deliberately light: the Nubble, one treat, maybe one additional coastal stop if the day is still feeling good. We leave some Maine unvisited.
